title: Unpin affinity locks during maintenance causing suppression of short requests in Private deployment
creator: Asha Patel
description: Customer ACME Telecom reported repeated 99th-percentile latency spikes for short (<=128 token) requests on their Private deployment immediately following weekly maintenance windows. Investigation showed small requests were being delayed or queued behind long-context flows for several seconds, causing user-facing timeouts and pager escalations. The issue is reproducible under mixed-length traffic when a maintenance window causes host-level prefetch/replication activity.
observations: Spike onset correlated with maintenance window start time (hosts doing KV shard rebalancing)
Telemetry shows a persistent 'affinity_lock' tag on several hosts after long-context requests complete
Admission/continuous-batcher kept inflight reservations for prefetch slots beyond end-of-request in mixed-length queues
Affected tenants showed rapid drop in short-request throughput while long requests consumed batching slots
root_cause: A race between maintenance-triggered KV prefetch/replication and the placement-affinity code: affinity locks (used to keep KV cache warm for long-context flows) were not cleared on request completion when maintenance triggered ephemeral host replicas. This left the scheduler believing those in-flight reservations still required the host, preventing admission for short flows and amplifying tail latency.
steps_taken: Reached out to ACME SRE; collected request traces and sampling tokens
Reproduced locally by running mixed-length load with simulated maintenance (kv-rebalance script)
Added adhoc telemetry to mark affinity_lock timestamps and lifetimes
Implemented a staged hotfix: clear affinity locks on completion + TTL guard for prefetch reservations
Opened PR with unit + integration tests and staging run (see PR link)
testing_summary: Unit tests added for affinity_lock lifecycle (pass)
Integration test simulating maintenance + mixed-length traffic (staging): short-request P99 reduced from 5.3s -> 120ms
Canary run (10% of internal traffic) ran for 24h with no regressions observed
rollout_plan: Canary 5% (2 hosts) -> 25% after 2h healthy -> 100% after 24h. Rollback via config toggle 'affinity-lock-clear=false'. Monitor P50/P95/P99, ingress QPS for short flows, and KV miss rates.
mitigation_for_customers: Temporary mitigation: requested ACME to throttle heavy long-context jobs during maintenance windows
Applied emergency config on their Private control plane to reduce prefetch parallelism for the maintenance window
review_feedback: Security: confirmed no secrets or KMS ops changed (security review not required)
Performance: add microbenchmark for affinity TTL rollback (in progress)
Product: add console alert when affinity_lock retention > 10s for a host
resolution: Hotfix merged to runtime-2.4.1 branch. Staging and canary validation show P99 short-request latency restored to expected levels. Long-term follow-ups scheduled.
postmortem_actions: ENG: implement admission preemption window to prioritize short flows during mixed-length waves (ENG-24999)
ENG: add automatic affinity_lock TTL and telemetry alerting (ENG-24900)
PM: document recommended maintenance patterns for Private customers to avoid prefetch storms
DX: surface maintenance-induced latency warnings in Console (console-2026.03)
SRE: run scheduled chaos tests for maintenance scenarios in staging
next_actions: Merge remaining scheduler tests and run full regression suite (assigned)
Execute controlled canary to customer Private clusters next maintenance window
Coordinate with solutions engineering to outreach to any other impacted high-QPS customers
